This file produces every figure and table for the final LaTeX report.

## Variables of interest

- **Genes:** *PTX3* (from Submission 1), *CXCR2*, and *RUNDC3A*
- **Continuous covariate:** maternal baseline 25-hydroxyvitamin D (ng/mL)
- **Additional continuous covariates (Table 1, NEW):** maternal age (years) and BMI (kg/m^2)
- **Categorical covariate 1:** pregnancy outcome (Normal vs Preeclampsia)
- **Categorical covariate 2 (derived from continuous):** vitamin D status
  (Deficient < 20, Insufficient 20-29.9, Sufficient 30+ ng/mL)

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# set some requirements for figures
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5, dpi = 300)
```

```{r packages}
library(tidyverse)   
library(kableExtra)  # Latex summary table
library(pheatmap)    # for clustered heatmap
```

# 1. Load the raw files

```{r load}
# Raw files, unchanged from Canvas
covar     <- read_csv("data/GSE85307_covar-1.csv")
expr      <- read_csv("data/GSE85307_geneExpression.csv")
geneNames <- read_csv("data/GSE85307_geneNames.csv")
```

## 2. Clean the covariate data (same steps as Submission 1)

Each covariate value is stored as text such as `"bmi_kg/m2: 37.52"`, so keep only the part after `": "` and convert numbers to numeric.

```{r clean-covar, results = "hide"}
covar_clean <- covar |> 
  # Rename first column name by position
  rename(subjectID = 1) |> 
  # For every column except the IDs, keep only the text after ": "; consulted
  # the help of Claude for this step to help with str_removal, detecting patterns
  mutate(across(-c(subjectID, geoID),
                ~ str_remove(.x, "^.*: "))) |> 
  # Convert the continuous variables from text to numeric
  mutate(across(c(mat_age_yrs, 
                  delivery_gestAge_wks, 
                  sampleCollection_gestAge_wks,
                  mat_BMI, 
                  mat_vitD), 
                as.numeric)) |> 
  mutate(
    # Pregnancy outcome as a factor, with normal and preeclampsia levels
    preg_preeclampsia = factor(preg_preeclampsia, 
                               levels = c("Normal", "Preeclampsia")),
    # Turn asthma into a labeled factor, either 0 or 1
    mat_asthma = factor(mat_asthma, 
                        levels = c("0", "1"), 
                        labels = c("Healthy", "Asthma")),
    # convert to factor variable
    batch_Microarray = factor(batch_Microarray),
    # turn continuous mat_vitD to categorical vitD_status variable
    # chose the intervals and cutoffs based off of existing clinical studies
    # and standard medical practices
    vitD_status = cut(mat_vitD,
                      breaks = c(-Inf, 20, 30, Inf),
                      right  = FALSE,   
                      labels = c("Deficient (<20)", 
                                 "Insufficient (20-29.9)", 
                                 "Sufficient (30+)"))
  )

summary(covar_clean)
count(covar_clean, preg_preeclampsia, vitD_status)
```

Sample size check for Methods section later. Final sample size and justification for removing any data points.

```{r sample-size}
# 157 samples, no missing values, and one sample per subject,
# so no samples need to be removed
nrow(covar_clean)
sum(is.na(covar_clean))
n_distinct(covar_clean$subjectID)
```

## 3. Build a long data frame with all of the genes
Building a data frame that holds every gene, because the function needs a data frame, so it can pull out whichever genes it is given.

```{r long-data, results = "hide"}
expr_long <- expr |> 
  # Probe ID column has no header; name it so it can be joined
  rename(PROBEID = 1) |> 
  # Attach gene names from the linker file
  left_join(geneNames, by = "PROBEID") |> 
  # convert to long format, so one row per gene per sample
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("GSM"),
               names_to  = "geoID",
               values_to = "expression")

# double check that every probe has a gene name, and no gene appears twice
sum(is.na(expr_long$GENE))
expr_long |>  
  distinct(PROBEID, GENE) |>  
  count(GENE) |>  
  filter(n > 1)  |>  
  nrow()
```

## 4. Merge with covariates and verify the match
```{r merge, results = "hide"}
# check if set of sample IDs in both files?
setequal(unique(expr_long$geoID), covar_clean$geoID)

analysis_long <- covar_clean |> 
  inner_join(expr_long, by = "geoID")

# Expect 157 samples x 500 genes = 78,500 rows, with 157 unique samples
# passed the check
nrow(analysis_long)
n_distinct(analysis_long$geoID)

# Check if merged PTX3 value for one sample equals the raw file value
analysis_long |> 
  filter(geoID == "GSM2264346", GENE == "PTX3")  |> 
  pull(expression)

expr |>  
  rename(PROBEID = 1)  |>  
  filter(PROBEID == 8083594)  |>  
  pull(GSM2264346)
```

## 5. Shared plot theme and colors (same from each previous submission)

```{r theme, results = "hide"}
# One theme for consistency across all plots; publication quality
theme_pub <- theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
        axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        legend.position = "top",
        legend.title = element_text(face = "bold"))

# shared colors
outcome_colors <- c("Normal" = "#4C72B0", "Preeclampsia" = "#C44E52")
```

## 6. Plotting function (same from Submission 2)

plot_genes() function takes the following inputs: a data frame and a vector of one or more gene names. For each gene it loops through, it makes the three Submission 1 plots (histogram, scatterplot vs vitamin D, boxplot by vitamin D status and outcome) and prints them, optionally saves them, and returns them in a named list.

```{r function}
# takes the input of a data frame, a vector of genes, into the figures directory
plot_genes <- function(df, genes, save = FALSE, out_dir = "figures") {

  # First initialize an empty list
  all_plots <- list()

  # Loop through each gene provided and produce the plots (huge for loop!)
  for (gene in genes) {
    
    # Keep only this gene's rows (one row per sample)
    # rename input data frame as gene_df
    gene_df <- df |>  
      filter(GENE == gene)
    # Axis label reused by all three plots
    y_lab <- paste(gene, "expression (log2 intensity)")
    
    # Plot 1: histogram showing distribution of expression; essentially same
    # code as submission 1
    p_hist <- ggplot(gene_df, aes(x = expression)) +
      # 0.05-wide bins suit the narrow range of log2 expression values
      geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.05, fill = "#3A7D7C", color = "white",
                     linewidth = 0.3) +
      # Dashed line at the median as a reference point
      geom_vline(aes(xintercept = median(expression)),
                 linetype = "dashed", color = "#1F2A37", linewidth = 0.6) +
      # Bars sit directly on the x-axis, with some space on top
      scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
      labs(title = paste("Distribution of", gene, "Expression"),
           x = y_lab,
           y = "Number of samples",
           caption = paste0("Dashed line = median; n = ", nrow(gene_df))) +
      theme_pub

    # Once again same thing but for plot 2: scatterplot of vitamin D 
    # vs expression. same code as submission 1, just changing the inputs.
    p_scatter <- ggplot(gene_df, aes(x = mat_vitD, y = expression)) +
      # One point per woman, colored by outcome
      geom_point(aes(color = preg_preeclampsia), alpha = 0.7, size = 2.5) +
      # Overall linear trend with 95% confidence band
      geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "black", se = TRUE) +
      scale_color_manual(values = outcome_colors) +
      labs(title = paste("Maternal Vitamin D vs", gene, "Expression"),
           x = "Maternal 25(OH)D at baseline (ng/mL)",
           y = y_lab,
           color = "Pregnancy outcome") +
      theme_pub

    # Same thing again, but for plot 3: boxplot by both categorical variables
    p_box <- ggplot(gene_df, aes(x = vitD_status, y = expression,
                                 fill = preg_preeclampsia)) +
      # Boxes side by side for each outcome; hide outliers because
      # all points are drawn below
      geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.8,
                   position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
      # Individual women, jittered sideways and aligned with their box
      geom_point(position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.15,
                                                 dodge.width  = 0.8),
                 size = 1.2, alpha = 0.6) +
      scale_fill_manual(values = outcome_colors) +
      # edit in that particular looped gene
      labs(title = paste(gene, "Expression by Vitamin D Status and Outcome"),
           x = "Maternal vitamin D status (ng/mL)",
           y = y_lab,
           fill = "Pregnancy outcome") +
      theme_pub

    # Print all three plots so they appear in the knitted document
    print(p_hist)
    print(p_scatter)
    print(p_box)

    # Save the plots named by gene if save is set to TRUE, the default input
    # is that save is set as FALSE initially; this is optional, that way doesn't
    # continuously rewrite plots each time functino is run
    if (save) {
      ggsave(file.path(out_dir, paste0("histogram_", gene, ".png")),
             p_hist, width = 7, height = 5, dpi = 300)
      ggsave(file.path(out_dir, paste0("scatter_vitD_", gene, ".png")),
             p_scatter, width = 7, height = 5, dpi = 300)
      ggsave(file.path(out_dir, paste0("boxplot_vitD_outcome_", gene, ".png")),
             p_box, width = 8, height = 5, dpi = 300)
    }

    # Store this gene's plots in the list under the gene's name
    # This way when the loop finishes you can pull out any single plot later
    # without rerunning the function
    all_plots[[gene]] <- list(histogram = p_hist,
                              scatter   = p_scatter,
                              boxplot   = p_box)
  }
}
```

## 7. Run the function on three genes

```{r run-function, fig.height = 5}
# interested genes in the list
genes_of_interest <- c("PTX3", "CXCR2", "RUNDC3A")

# Set save = TRUE to save the 9 figures in figures folder
# Set save = FALSE in final pdf/markdown because don't want to keep running
# this over and over

# takes the analysis_long data frame input created from step 3 and 4 as input
# also takes list genes in previous line as input
gene_plots <- plot_genes(analysis_long, genes_of_interest, save = FALSE)
```

## 8. Summary statistics for the three genes

Statistics cited in the Results section for each gene: median and SD of
expression, Spearman correlation with vitamin D, and p-values for outcome
(Wilcoxon) and vitamin D status (Kruskal-Wallis).

```{r gene-stats}
gene_stats <- analysis_long |>
  filter(GENE %in% genes_of_interest) |>
  group_by(GENE) |>
  summarise(
    median_expr = median(expression),
    sd_expr     = sd(expression),
    rho_vitD    = cor(expression, mat_vitD, method = "spearman"),
    p_vitD      = cor.test(expression, mat_vitD, method = "spearman",
                           exact = FALSE)$p.value,
    p_outcome   = wilcox.test(expression ~ preg_preeclampsia)$p.value,
    p_vitD_cat  = kruskal.test(expression ~ vitD_status)$p.value
  )

gene_stats |> mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 3)))
```

## 9. Summary statistics for the table
Three continuous covariates (vitamin D, maternal age, BMI) shown as mean (SD)
and two categorical covariates (pregnancy outcome as the strata, vitamin D
status) shown as n (%). P-values: Welch t-test for continuous covariates and
chi-square test for vitamin D status.

```{r table1-continuous}
# mean (SD) of each continuous covariate for all women (Overall column)
covar_clean |> 
  summarise(across(c(mat_vitD, mat_age_yrs, mat_BMI),
                   list(mean = mean, sd = sd))) |> 
  mutate(across(everything(), ~ round(.x, 1)))

# mean (SD) of each continuous covariate by pregnancy outcome
covar_clean |> 
  group_by(preg_preeclampsia) |> 
  summarise(across(c(mat_vitD, mat_age_yrs, mat_BMI),
                   list(mean = mean, sd = sd))) |> 
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 1)))

# p-values comparing normal vs preeclampsia (Welch t-test)
t.test(mat_vitD    ~ preg_preeclampsia, data = covar_clean)$p.value
t.test(mat_age_yrs ~ preg_preeclampsia, data = covar_clean)$p.value
t.test(mat_BMI     ~ preg_preeclampsia, data = covar_clean)$p.value
```

```{r table1-categorical}
# n (%) in each vitamin D status for all women (Overall column)
covar_clean |> 
  count(vitD_status) |> 
  mutate(percent = round(100 * n / sum(n)))

# n (%) in each vitamin D status within each pregnancy outcome
covar_clean |> 
  count(preg_preeclampsia, vitD_status) |> 
  group_by(preg_preeclampsia) |> 
  mutate(percent = round(100 * n / sum(n)))

# p-value: does vitamin D status differ by outcome? (chi-square test)
chisq.test(table(covar_clean$vitD_status,
                 covar_clean$preg_preeclampsia))$p.value
```

## 10. Heatmap of 10 genes with tracking bars

The three genes of interest plus the seven most variable remaining genes. Each
gene is z-scored across samples so genes with different expression levels share
one color scale.

```{r}
# 7 most variable genes, not counting the 3 genes of interest
top_var_genes <- analysis_long |> 
  filter(!GENE %in% genes_of_interest) |> 
  group_by(GENE) |> 
  summarise(variance = var(expression)) |> 
  arrange(desc(variance)) |> 
  slice_head(n = 7) |> 
  pull(GENE)

heatmap_genes <- c(genes_of_interest, top_var_genes)
```

```{r}
# matrix with genes as rows and samples as columns
heat_mat <- analysis_long |> 
  filter(GENE %in% heatmap_genes) |> 
  select(GENE, geoID, expression) |> 
  pivot_wider(names_from = geoID, values_from = expression) |> 
  column_to_rownames("GENE") |> 
  as.matrix()

# tracking bars: one row per sample, row names = sample IDs
tracking <- covar_clean |> 
  select(geoID, Outcome = preg_preeclampsia, `Vitamin D` = vitD_status) |> 
  column_to_rownames("geoID")

# colors for the tracking bars
tracking_colors <- list(
  Outcome     = outcome_colors,
  `Vitamin D` = c("Deficient (<20)"        = "#F2C14E",
                  "Insufficient (20-29.9)" = "#9BBF85",
                  "Sufficient (30+)"       = "#3A7D7C"))

heat <- pheatmap(heat_mat,
                 scale = "row", # z-score each gene
                 clustering_method = "ward.D2",  # cluster genes and samples
                 annotation_col = tracking, # tracking bars
                 annotation_colors = tracking_colors,
                 show_colnames = FALSE, # 157 sample IDs unreadable
                 main = "Expression of 10 Genes (row z-scores)")

# save a copy
ggsave("figures/heatmap_10genes.png", heat, width = 9, height = 5.5, dpi = 300)
```

## 11. Additional plot: treemap of group sizes and expression

A treemap splits a rectangle into tiles whose area is proportional to a count.
Here each tile is one group of women (pregnancy outcome x vitamin D status), so
the tile area shows how many women are in that group. Tile color shows how
that group's median expression compares with the gene's overall median
(red = higher, blue = lower). 

```{r treemap, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 5}
library(treemapify)

treemap_df <- analysis_long |> 
  filter(GENE %in% genes_of_interest) |> 
  # expression relative to each gene's overall median, so all 3 genes
  # can share one color scale
  group_by(GENE) |> 
  mutate(rel_expr = expression - median(expression)) |> 
  # one row per gene x outcome x vitamin D status group
  group_by(GENE, preg_preeclampsia, vitD_status) |> 
  summarise(n = n(), median_rel = median(rel_expr), .groups = "drop") |> 
  mutate(GENE  = factor(GENE, levels = genes_of_interest), # panel order
         label = paste0(vitD_status, "\nn = ", n))  # tile label
```


```{r}
p_treemap <- ggplot(treemap_df, aes(area = n, fill = median_rel, label = label,
                                    subgroup = preg_preeclampsia)) +
  geom_treemap(color = "white") + # one tile per group
  geom_treemap_subgroup_border(color = "black", size = 3) + # outline each outcome
  geom_treemap_subgroup_text(place = "bottom", size = 12, # outcome label
                             fontface = "bold", alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_treemap_text(place = "topleft", size = 9, reflow = TRUE) + # group label
  # blue = lower, white = same, red = higher than the gene's median
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2C5D8A", mid = "#F7F7F7", high = "#B2343A",
                       midpoint = 0, limits = c(-0.35, 0.35),
                       name = "Group median minus\ngene median (log2)") +
  facet_wrap(~ GENE) + # one panel per gene
  labs(title = "Group Sizes and Relative Expression by Outcome and Vitamin D Status",
       caption = paste("Tile area is the number of women;",
                       "color is group median minus the gene's overall median")) +
  theme_pub +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
        strip.background = element_blank(),
        plot.title = element_text(size = 14),
        legend.key.width = unit(1.5, "cm"))

p_treemap

# save the figure
ggsave("figures/treemap_groups.png", p_treemap, width = 11, height = 5, dpi = 300)
```
